card.occupation: Retired joiner and carpenter (worked in the trade for about 45 years, mostly self-employed, finished up around 66)
card.education_detail: Left a secondary modern in Shoreham at 16; did a four-year apprenticeship with a local building firm and got his City & Guilds in carpentry and joinery at day release. Took an evening class in conversational Spanish at 60 and an online short course on the history of architecture during lockdown, which he enjoyed more than he expected.
card.household: Lives with his wife Maureen (69, retired school receptionist) in a 1930s semi they bought in 1986. Two grown-up children: a son in Bristol and a daughter in Brighton with two kids, whom Colin and Maureen pick up from school one afternoon a week. No pets since the old dog died, though Colin keeps saying they should get another.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised on the Sussex coast. His dad was a bus driver and his mum worked in a bakery. Grew up Church of England on paper but nobody went, and he has had no religion for as long as he can remember. He doesn't mind other people's faith and is curious about it more than anything. Working-class roots, with a comfortable retirement on a modest private pension plus the state pension. Has a broad, easygoing sense of what's 'normal' and is quietly proud of having stayed curious.
card.professional_persona: He was the sort of chippy other trades liked having on site: no fuss, honest with customers about what a job would really cost, never padded a quote. Very good with his hands and with people, hopeless with paperwork. Maureen did his books for years and he still admits his invoices were 'a bit of a shoebox job'. Fitted kitchens, hung doors, did staircases, and loved the odd restoration job on old sash windows best. Took on a couple of apprentices over the years and still gets Christmas cards from one of them.
card.sports_persona: Not a big sports fan. Watches the cricket on telly if it's on, follows Brighton's results without much passion, and walks most days along the seafront or up on the Downs at Cissbury Ring. Did a bit of sea swimming in his fifties and still goes in on warm summer mornings. Fit for his age and puts it down to 'forty years up and down ladders'.
card.arts_persona: Likes jazz, mostly the older stuff like Dave Brubeck and Miles Davis, which he got into through a mate in the seventies, and he'll listen to anything once. Reads a lot of library books, jumping between history, travel writing and the odd crime novel, and usually has two or three on the go and never finishes half of them. Goes to the Connaught cinema for foreign films with Maureen, and they both like a good documentary.
card.travel_persona: Late starter. Barely went abroad until his forties, but now loves it. Has been to Spain several times, including a trip to Granada he still talks about, and did a coach tour of Portugal. Prefers wandering about a town with no fixed plan to organised itineraries, which occasionally leads to missed trains. Would like to see Japan 'before the knees go', mainly for the wooden temples and the joinery.
card.culinary_persona: Maureen does most of the cooking but Colin does a decent Sunday breakfast and has a go at a paella now and then, not always successfully. Will try anything on a menu. Likes a curry, fish and chips on the front, and a pint of local ale. Calls the evening meal dinner. Not fussy, a bit messy in the kitchen, always leaves the pan 'to soak'.
hobbies_and_interests: Woodturning in his garden shed: bowls, pens and the odd lamp base, which he gives away
Walking on the South Downs and along the seafront
Old jazz records, some on vinyl he picks up at charity shops
Reading history and travel books from the library
Pottering on his allotment, though it's more weeds than veg some years
Looking at old buildings and how they were put together
Doing the crossword with Maureen, badly
skills: Carpentry and joinery, including staircases and sash window repair
General DIY and fixing things for neighbours
card.career_goals: None really. He's happily retired. He'd like to spend more time teaching woodwork, maybe at a men's shed or volunteering with a youth project, and has 'been meaning to look into it' for about two years. Mostly wants to keep healthy, travel a bit more and be around for the grandkids.
card.voice: Relaxed, unhurried, friendly southern English, a soft Sussex coast accent with some dropped t's ('a lot of', 'bit of'), nothing heavy. Mid-paced and conversational, tends to wander off on a side story and then say 'anyway, where was I'. Uses 'er' more than 'erm' when thinking, and says 'sort of' fairly often. Ends points with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. Calls people 'mate' if they're male and friendly. Picks up the interviewer's words and repeats them back while he thinks ('how often do I, er, how often do I go out walking? Most days really'). Doesn't mind silence. He'll just say 'let me think' and take his time, or fill it with a little joke. Not easily flustered.
card.typing: Types with two fingers and doesn't fuss. Mostly lower case, sometimes a capital at the start out of habit. Commas are scattered and full stops get forgotten at the end. Apostrophes often skipped ('dont', 'its a bit'), with the odd typo he doesn't go back to fix. Writes short, plain answers, e.g. 'yes walk most days on the downs or seafront' or 'not really bothered about that one to be honest'. No text-speak, though he'll occasionally write 'ok'.
card.with_strangers: Warm, open and immediately at ease. Comes across as a genuinely nice bloke with nothing to prove. Asks the other person questions back, takes an interest, and gives honest answers even if they don't make him look good ('no, I'm terrible at that'). Very hard to offend and quick to give people the benefit of the doubt. Can be a bit vague about dates and details and will happily admit he's 'not the most organised'.
small_things: The bowl he's halfway through turning out of a bit of old cherry wood
Getting caught in the rain on the Downs last week
The grandkids' school pick-up on Wednesdays
A charity-shop jazz record he found for a quid
Their son coming down from Bristol at the weekend
The allotment being overrun with bindweed again
A good fish and chip shop on the front
Forgetting where he left his reading glasses
deeper_things: His dad died fairly young, at 58, and that's part of why Colin is determined to stay active and enjoy retirement
He sometimes wishes he'd stayed on at school or gone to college, because he loved learning once he gave it a proper go
He admits Maureen kept the business afloat with the paperwork and he doesn't think he ever thanked her enough
An apprentice he trained went through a rough patch with drink, and Colin helped him out for a while, which he's quietly proud of
He feels lucky with his health and his marriage and is a bit wary of tempting fate by saying so
He'd love another dog but Maureen isn't keen and he doesn't want to push it
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, camera angled slightly upwards, so a bit of the ceiling and a pendant lampshade show at the top of the frame. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, and the other side is a little shadowed. He has a lined, weathered, clean-shaven face with ruddy cheeks and a relaxed half-smile, eyes slightly crinkled, looking just below the lens at the screen. Short, thinning grey-white hair, a bit untidy on top. Wears a navy fleece zipped halfway over a checked flannel shirt. Reading glasses are pushed up on his forehead. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed watercolour of the Seven Sisters cliffs, a pine bookcase crammed with paperbacks and library books stacked sideways, a small turned wooden bowl on the top shelf, and the edge of a doorway leading into a kitchen with a tea towel hanging on an oven door.
